rfm_tuples.R: In December 2023, we made the decision to significantly reduce the size of our global EV fleet and initiated EV vehicle dispositions ... Our decision to reduce our EV fleet resulted in the recognition, during the fourth quarter of 2023, of $245 million of incremental net depreciation expense related to the sale. (10-K, Item 1A)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify the $245M charge appears in FY2023 financials and the disposition plan reads as a discrete, bounded action. Mode B: derive whether the disposal completes cleanly or expands (a discrete 'one-time' EV cut vs. ongoing serial impairment); check Q1 2024 10-Q (htzz-20240331) for follow-on disposal groups.
rfm_tuples.M_value: In March 2024 the Company identified a 'Second EV Disposal Group' (~9,000 Americas + ~1,000 International EVs); Q1 2024 write-downs $107M Americas + $7M International = $114M on Second Group, plus additional $81M loss/write-down on remaining First Group. Q1 2024 total 'depreciation of revenue earning vehicles & lease charges, net' = $969M vs $381M YoY (+154%).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K framed the EV cut as a discrete Q4 2023 action with $245M charge. 10 weeks later, a Second Disposal Group adds $114M more in writedowns, indicating the EV residual problem is open-ended, not contained. Classic 'one more quarter' pattern.

rfm_tuples.R: Depreciation Per Unit Per Month ... is reflective of how we are managing the costs of our vehicles. (10-K MD&A non-GAAP metric)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: re-derive the Americas RAC Depreciation Per Unit Per Month from FY2023 segment data; Mode B: trend the metric Q1 2023 vs Q1 2024 to see if EV writedowns are an isolated 'lump' or systemic depreciation acceleration.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Americas RAC Depreciation Per Unit Per Month: Q1 2023 $282 -> Q1 2024 $649 (+130%, 'NM' flagged). International RAC: $120 -> $326 (+172%, 'NM' flagged). Both segments simultaneously.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: A doubling/tripling of the company's own management KPI in a single quarter is not 'management of costs'; it is a residual-value reset. The fact that both segments move together suggests broader fleet residual marks, not just EV-specific.

rfm_tuples.R: Hertz was in compliance with the First Lien Ratio [3.0x Q1/Q4, 3.5x Q2/Q3]. (10-K Note on First Lien Credit Agreement covenants)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm compliance as of 12/31/2023. Mode B: check whether the company sought relief on this covenant near cutoff — covenant amendments are the strongest distress tell.
rfm_tuples.M_value: On April 16, 2024, THC entered into Amendment No. 8 to Credit Agreement, which (i) raises the First Lien Leverage Ratio to 5.0x in Q2/Q3 2024 and 4.75x in Q4 2024/Q1 2025 (vs. baseline 3.0-3.5x), (ii) adds a NEW minimum liquidity covenant ($400M monthly Q2-Q3 2024, $500M monthly Q4 2024-Q1 2025), (iii) restricts Restricted Payments and Permitted Investments. Sunsets only at start of Q2 2025.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: A covenant amendment that simultaneously (a) raises max leverage by ~66%, (b) imposes a new minimum-liquidity floor, and (c) freezes restricted payments is textbook 'pre-distress' relief obtained from lenders. Sunset 2Q25 = lenders give one year to fix it.

rfm_tuples.R: The 2022 Share Repurchase Program ... authorized additional repurchases of up to an incremental $2.0 billion. (10-K and Q1 10-Q)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm program exists. Mode B: derive whether the program continues to operate or is being constrained by other actions.
rfm_tuples.M_source: edgar_10q Q1 2024 Note on Stockholders' Equity
rfm_tuples.M_value: 'However, during the effective period of Amendment No. 8 ... the repurchase of shares is not permitted commencing April 16, 2024 through April 1, 2025.' Q1 2024 share repurchases = $0 (vs $101M in Q1 2023).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital-return program suspended by lender mandate. Combined with C3 this confirms creditors, not management, are setting the capital allocation rules — a major step toward distress.

rfm_tuples.R: Our cash flows from operations, together with amounts available under various liquidity facilities and refinancing options available to us in the capital markets, will be sufficient to fund our operating activities and obligations for the next twelve months and for the foreseeable future thereafter. (10-K and Q1 10-Q liquidity statement)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: validate cash + facility availability. Mode B: trend unrestricted cash and check whether the new $400M-$500M minimum liquidity covenant constrains usable cash.
rfm_tuples.M_source: edgar_10q Q1 2024 balance sheet and cash flow statement
rfm_tuples.M_value: Unrestricted cash: $764M (12/31/23) -> $465M (3/31/24), -$299M / -39% in one quarter. Total cash + restricted: $1,206M -> $945M, -$261M. First Lien RCF drawn $450M (vs $0 at 12/31/23). Minimum liquidity covenant kicks in Q2 2024 at $400M; with unrestricted at $465M the cushion vs covenant is only ~$65M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 12-month liquidity claim is technically true but the buffer to the brand-new covenant floor is razor-thin. Drawing the RCF $450M in one quarter while losing $300M cash is a classic late-cycle liquidity-defense pattern. Mode B catches what the disclosure obscures.

rfm_tuples.R: On March 12, 2024, Stephen M. Scherr ... notified the Company of his decision to resign as Chief Executive Officer ... Mr. Scherr's resignation was not because of any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to the Company's operations, policies or practices. (8-K 2024-03-18)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm boilerplate 'no disagreement' wording. Mode B: check timing/cluster with other governance departures; CEO resignations 'voluntarily' (forfeiting severance) ~5 weeks after $245M EV charge and ~4 weeks before covenant relief amendment are not benign.
rfm_tuples.M_source: edgar 8-K cluster: 2024-03-18 (CEO Scherr resign 3/31), 2024-03-22 (director Bermanzohn resign), 2024-04-03 (GC Batcheler resign 4/10)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Three senior departures in ~3 weeks: CEO/Chair, a director (~14 months on board), and EVP/General Counsel/Secretary. CEO forfeited severance ('voluntarily resigning ... not entitled to any post-termination severance'). New CEO Wayne West (ex-Cruise COO/ex-Delta COO) hired with $33M sign-on, guaranteed bonus ≥112.5% of base for 2024.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: CEO/director/GC cluster departure ~30 days before lenders impose covenant relief + buyback ban is a classic 'house cleaning before the bad news cycle' pattern. The CEO forfeiting severance is unusual and suggests dispute or constructive exit even with boilerplate 'no disagreement' language. Mode B finding.

rfm_tuples.R: We offer a diverse fleet of EVs through agreements with a variety of EV manufactures, such as Tesla, Polestar and General Motors. (10-K Item 1)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm relationships exist (qualitative). Mode B: derive whether residual-value exposure is concentrated in any one OEM whose used pricing has been pressured (Tesla cut new prices repeatedly through 2023-Q1 2024 per filings cross-references), and whether 'diverse' is contradicted by concentration in the disposal groups.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1A and Q1 2024 10-Q Note 4 disposal group disclosures
rfm_tuples.M_value: Disposal groups specifically tied to 'a decline in EV residual values' and 'elevated EV damage and collision costs.' First Disposal Group carrying value $542M; Second Group $227M Americas + $30M Intl = $257M. ~19,000 EVs at disposal across both groups. Disclosures do not name a specific OEM but emphasize Americas RAC concentration (~90% of disposal vehicles).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Company avoids naming the OEM concentration. Cannot fully verify within blinding; flagged for residual-OEM-concentration risk but not scored as severe absent direct disclosure.

rfm_tuples.R: /s/ Ernst & Young LLP ... We have served as the Company's auditor since 2019. (10-K auditor report, Tampa, Florida, February 12, 2024)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify auditor identity, tenure, opinion type. Mode B: check for critical audit matters (CAMs) or qualifications.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Ernst & Young LLP (Big 4), unqualified opinion, no going-concern qualification, tenure since 2019. CAMs include liability reserves (insurance) — standard for vehicle rental. No auditor resignation or disagreement found in 8-K stream pre-cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Clean Big 4 auditor relationship; no audit-side red flag. This is one of the few PASS signals.

rfm_tuples.R: Net income (loss) attributable to Hertz Global $616 million for 2023 (10-K) ... Net income (loss) Q1 2024 = ($186) million (Hertz Global) / ($272) million (Hertz Corp) (Q1 10-Q)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: arithmetic check on the swing. Mode B: derive whether the swing is concentrated in EV / fleet items or pervasive across operations.
rfm_tuples.M_source: edgar_10k FY2023 income statement, edgar_10q Q1 2024 income statement
rfm_tuples.M_value: Y/Y swing Q1 2024 vs Q1 2023: Hertz Global $196M -> ($186M), a $382M deterioration. Hertz Corp: $314M -> ($272M), a $586M deterioration. EV-related charges (~$114M Second Group + ~$81M First Group) = ~$195M, only about half the swing. Remainder is depreciation acceleration, lower volume/pricing, and higher interest.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The narrative blames EVs, but EV charges explain only ~50% of the loss swing. Underlying core rental economics also deteriorated meaningfully Y/Y. Mode B exposes that 'it's just the EV thing' framing is incomplete.

rfm_tuples.R: HVF III Series 2021-1 ... $2,000 million ... 12/2024 maturity (Q1 10-Q debt schedule); HVF III Series 2021-A Class A notes amended in April 2024 to extend maturity to April 2026 (Q1 10-Q debt note).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify the maturity wall. Mode B: derive whether near-term ABS maturities (within 12 months of cutoff) are pre-funded or expose the company to refinancing risk at distressed spreads.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Within 12 months of 2024-05-15 cutoff: HVF III Series 2021-1 $2.0B (Dec 2024 maturity), HVF III Series 2021-A Class A $1.5B+ (originally June 2025; extended to April 2026 in April 2024), HVF III Series 2022-1 $750M (June 2025). Series 2021-A Class B $188M August 2025 fixed at 9.44%. April 2024 European ABS upsized 1.2B -> 1.3B. Senior Notes Due 2026 $500M fixed 4.625%; due 2029 $1.0B fixed 5.0%. First Lien RCF drawn $450M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: ABS maturity tower with $2.0B due Dec 2024 is being actively re-termed (HVF III Series 2021-A extension Apr 2024 is a tell). Senior unsecured notes are still at low fixed coupons (4.625% / 5.0%), so the bond stack is not yet repriced — meaning the distress isn't fully marked at the corporate level. Refinancing the $2B Dec 2024 ABS at 2024 spreads is the near-term overhang.

supplemental_signals.going_concern_language: Standard 'continue as a going concern' boilerplate only; NO 'substantial doubt' language in 10-K or Q1 10-Q. Severity: PASS on text, but disclosure-vs-reality gap is captured in C3/C5.
supplemental_signals.stock_drawdown_context: -71.3% trailing drawdown at cutoff, with the distress signals concentrated in the 90 days pre-cutoff (Q4 2023 $245M charge -> Feb 12 10-K -> CEO/GC departures Mar 12-Apr 3 -> Amendment No. 8 Apr 16 -> Q1 10-Q Apr 25 with Second EV Group and depreciation/unit doubling).
supplemental_signals.insider_form4_cluster: 20 Form 4s in 6 months pre-cutoff; cluster Apr 1-3, 2024 (5 filings) coincides with new CEO equity grant. Heavy 3/5/2024 and 5/3/2024 filings warrant directional analysis (not done here due to blinding budget).
supplemental_signals.mode_b_topline: Mode B yielded the strongest signals: (i) EV disposal group expansion not present in 10-K, (ii) Depreciation Per Unit Per Month doubling/tripling, (iii) Amendment No. 8 covenant relief + buyback ban, (iv) governance cluster timed to bracket bad-news quarter, (v) net loss swing 2x larger than EV explanation.

summary: Hertz at 2024-05-15 displays a textbook late-cycle distress profile that the FY2023 10-K substantially understated. The 10-K framed the EV write-down as a discrete $245M Q4 action; ten weeks later the Q1 2024 10-Q discloses a 'Second EV Disposal Group' with another $114M of charges and total fleet depreciation per unit doubling in Americas and tripling in International — the EV problem is open-ended, not contained. Simultaneously, lenders imposed Amendment No. 8 (Apr 16, 2024) raising the First Lien Leverage Ratio to 5.0x, adding a new $400-500M minimum liquidity covenant, and freezing share repurchases through Apr 1, 2025 — a creditor-driven capital lockdown. CEO Scherr resigned forfeiting severance, the GC and a director also departed in a 3-week cluster bracketing the bad news. Unrestricted cash fell from $764M to $465M in one quarter, leaving only ~$65M of cushion above the new covenant floor. Auditor (E&Y, Big 4, since 2019) is clean and there is no 'substantial doubt' wording, but the gap between 10-K narrative ('we will be sufficient') and Q1 reality is severe. This name is OBSCURING, not lying outright. Verdict: SHORT-tier.
